featured_reviews.name: Sid The Explorer
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had visited here for voluntary blood donation. The experience was very good as the staff were courteous and professional.
During the donation I felt a bit uneasy, and the staff handled it promptly and calmly.
After the donation, they offered Frooti and provided a certificate, donor card, and a bottle as a memento, which felt thoughtful. Since I was not feeling fully normal, they also asked me to wait at reception for a few minutes and leave only after I felt completely fine.
The place is well maintained and is only a 5 to 7 minute walk from Goregaon West railway station. I would definitely recommend it for blood donation.

Highly recommended for anyone considering blood donation!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited the hospital for blood donation with a genuine intention to help others. During the screening, I was told that my hemoglobin level was low. However, after further tests, everything came out normal and there was no health issue found.

I feel the staff handling the blood donation process need better training and proper knowledge. Hiring inexperienced staff without enough medical understanding can create unnecessary fear and confusion for donors. Because of this, people who come forward for a good cause may feel discouraged from donating blood again.

I hope the hospital management improves staff training and ensures accurate guidance is given to donors in the future.

Fortunately we did not need blood on 20.03 and 21.03 but we were in need of blood unit for 22.03.2026.When we called them, they said it is over 24 hours so you will have to pay deposit again . Basically a con game to get ₹450 as advance and refuse to accept it later ( within 48 hours). This is absolute inhuman behaviour from the blood bank. They will have a curse of a million people if they continue to operate with such foolish money mindset with no respect to customer inconvenience and do not bother to give any receipts or  explain these terms before making reservation. They should be closed down on unethical business practices.

featured_reviews.name: Dwiti Thakkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have voluntarily donated blood in this blood bank couple of times , however last afternoon I got a call from them stating that they have an emergency blood requirement, and if I can donate blood , I agreed, they said that I can either go by 4:00pm or tomorrow morning by 9am, since it was already 3:30 when they called and i wouldn't be able to reach in time I decided to go next morning 9am . When I reached no staff was there at the reception the two sisters were inside the ward which was a restricted area and were listening to music. I called them out loud but they didn't listen as they were engrossed in their music, i thought to call the landline, they completely ignored the landline, after waiting for 15 mins both the sisters came out. I told them I had got a call that there's an emergency hence have come for voluntary blood donation. However I was menstruating so will it be ok i donate blood. They told me they weren't aware so to wait for doctors who come at 9:30. I again waited till the doctor's arrived. None of the doctors cared to call me inside even knowing that I was waiting. After a while I asked the nurse if I could now go inside. There were 2 docs, one male n one female. Disappointed , pathetic experience!!
On 6th Mar'24 , I visited Dr.Madhulika Goyle - Verified  & booked by Practo for a basic health fitness certificate for learning swimming lessons.

On my 1st visit on 6th Mar'24, like any other patient I just observed from my patient seat as I trusted the doctor that she has mentioned my correct name & has signed stamped. Then I just took the certificate envelope & left. Later when I finally got the time to enroll the classes & was approaching my swimming class I was surprised this so-called 17years experienced doctor is so absent minded that  she certified me back dated 6/2/23 . I too have other work & commitments then later I manage to pay a personal visit & sort this but her clinic was closed till 13th May'24 .So on 20th May'24, I searched through Practo & again booked appointment & contacted her about the issue. After learning that it was her fault she told me to cancel Practo booking else Practo will charge as both , she insisted & I cancelled my practo booking.

Then 20th May'24 evening when I visited this clinic, to my surprise this doctor was very unprofessionally , sounding like a vegetable vendor mentioned 4-5 times that she on goodwill is doing these changes , trusting on me that it's her fault and not charging me any fees, but otherwise to make date changes I need to pay her fees. Later when I was packing she grabbed my old certificate (dated 6/2/23 ) saying that I need to return it to her & take this new one. I have seen no doctor treating their patient this way. Still I requested her as she was out of town for more than 15-20days, kindly make my new certificate 15days ahead from my actual first visit date which was 6th Mar'24. She started bargaining with me for a new certificate that I need to pay. I just heard her & left her clinic with my old certificate.

First of all she is a doctor, she needs to behave professionally , politely & not like a local vendor negotiating with a patient for fees, secondly it was her fault that her absent minded cost me Rs.800 for 1st visit fees where she wrote a year back dated certificate & because of her I didn't enroll my classes (now it would have been more than 30 days of my swimming sessions) as I was not having time to visit her & get a revised certificate.
Also, I always saw this clinic not operational, no patients, no receptionist even both the times I booked and she visited only that time, how can Practo put a profile of such a doctor on an esteemed site?

I am posting my review so that no other patient in need is misleaded.

featured_reviews.name: jay sanghavi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Title: Disappointed with Lack of Discounts for Regular Blood Donations

Review:

I have been an active blood donor for several years, and I have participated in numerous blood donation camps organized by various organizations. While I appreciate the efforts made by ANVISHKA (GHATKOPAR WEST MUMBAI ) in collecting and distributing blood, I am deeply disappointed by the lack of recognition and benefits given to regular donors like myself.

Throughout the years, I have diligently donated my blood, always carrying my proof cards as evidence of my contributions. However, despite my consistent efforts, I have never received any discounts on blood when I required it during my own medical emergencies. I find this disheartening, as it seems that ANVISHKA does not value the loyalty and dedication of the blood donors

It is not unreasonable to expect some form of acknowledgment or incentive for those of us who selflessly give our blood to help others. Other blood banks and organizations often provide discounts or priority access to regular donors, recognizing their commitment and encouraging them to continue their vital contributions.

I sincerely hope that ANVISHKA takes this feedback into consideration and reevaluates their policies regarding discounts for regular blood donors. Acknowledging and rewarding the generosity of individuals who consistently support their cause would not only foster a stronger bond with the donor community but also motivate others to become regular blood donors.

I still believe in the importance of blood donation and will continue to contribute to the cause, but I hope ANVISHKA reconsiders their stance on recognizing the dedication of their regular donors.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant Tawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently donated blood at this blood bank and was informed that my blood had tested positive for hepatitis C antibodies using the ELISA Generation 4 method. Naturally, this news was extremely concerning, so I took it upon myself to get retested at a private lab. The private lab conducted two tests—one using the rapid method and the other using the ELFA method. Both of these tests came back negative for hepatitis C antibodies. To be absolutely sure, I also did an HCV RNA PCR test, which is the most reliable test for detecting an active hepatitis C infection. Thankfully, the result was "NOT DETECTED," meaning there was no active virus in my blood.

This whole experience has caused me unnecessary stress and confusion. I fully understand that antibody tests can sometimes give false positives, but I believe the blood bank should be more cautious and thorough before alarming donors with such serious results. Furthermore, after receiving the initial notification, I reached out to the blood bank multiple times seeking guidance on what to do next, but they have stopped responding to my queries. They haven’t provided any further support, leaving me in the dark about whether I can donate blood in the future or what steps I should take.

This lack of communication and support from the blood bank is extremely disappointing, especially when dealing with such sensitive health concerns. I advise others to be cautious and double-check their results if they receive any alarming notifications from this blood bank. I hope the blood bank improves their processes, both in terms of accuracy and in providing proper guidance to donors.
